description: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. ABOUT THE TEAM Advanced Capabilities is the internal warfighter research team for Anduril's Maneuver Dominance division. We invent new products, inform vehicle specifications, define autonomous tactics, and work out how humans and teams of autonomous systems will operate together in future contested multi-domain environments. You'll join a small, multinational team of engineers spanning multiple disciplines such as wargaming, game engineering, HPC simulations, LLM agents and VR environments; all to give our warfighters and researchers the leverage to explore faster, test more ideas, and better understand tomorrow’s war. ABOUT THE ROLE We are building the next generation of wargaming facilities purpose-built for the military to run massive-scale simulations of autonomous systems operating in contested environments. Those facilities are only useful if they are up, current, and trustworthy. A failed scenario run or a silent regression after a software release costs operators and engineers’ real time. As our founding Site Reliability Engineer, you will design, build, and operate the infrastructure that makes this possible. You'll work at the intersection of hardware, simulation software and distributed systems. You will be the person who knows why the simulation broke, who catches it before anyone else notices, and who makes sure it doesn't break the same way twice. This is a hands-on role that blends software maintenance, infrastructure ownership, and release validation, with direct exposure to the development teams whose code you're keeping stable. This position is in Abu Dhabi, UAE, with initial position hiring occurring in London, UK. Candidate must be willing to relocate to the facility upon completion. WHAT YOU'LL DO Maintain the simulation software stack - installation, configuration, updates, version management, and day-to-day functionality across the Simulation Center's tools and environments. Own the underlying infrastructure - compute, networking, storage, and environment configuration that the simulation depends on; keep it provisioned, patched, and performant. Build and maintain a post-release test suite - design, automate, and continually extend a regression and smoke-test process that runs after every software release or configuration change, so integration issues surface immediately rather than mid-exercise. Forecast, diagnose, and eliminate failure modes - root-cause errors and bugs in the system, drive them to permanent resolution, and implement the guardrails, monitoring, or process changes that prevent recurrence. Partner with development teams and stakeholders - review upcoming changes for reliability risk, surface concerns early, and implement mitigation strategies before releases land in the simulation environment. Monitor overall system health - instrument and watch the environment, triage issues within your scope, and escalate clearly and quickly with the context needed for others to act when an issue exceeds your ability to resolve it. Document what you learn - runbooks, known issues, environment configuration, and release validation results, so the Simulation Center's operational knowledge isn't held in one person's head. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Proficiency in Python for automation, tooling, and test development. Working knowledge of C++; enough to read, debug, build, and trace issues in the simulation codebase. Solid general networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, UDP, multicast, DNS, routing, firewalls, and the ability to diagnose latency, packet loss, and connectivity problems across distributed systems. Experience with project management, issue tracking, bug triage, and coordinating work across engineering teams. Demonstrated experience maintaining production or production-adjacent systems, including troubleshooting under time pressure. Strong written and verbal communication; you can escalate an issue, explain a root cause, and write a runbook someone else can follow. Eligibility to pass the security and background check requirements for sensitive information systems. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience with modeling and simulation, wargaming, or distributed simulation standards (DIS, HLA, TENA) and platforms such as AFSIM, VBS, or similar. Test automation and CI/CD experience; building automated validation pipelines, not just running them. Infrastructure-as-code and configuration management (Terraform, Ansible, Docker, Kubernetes). On-prem and cloud deployment experience. Observability tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, or equivalent. Linux systems administration depth; comfort in mixed Linux/Windows environments. Prior work in a defense, aerospace, or classified environment. Active security clearance. title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Simulation
description: Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. The Simulator team builds state-of-the-art simulations of realistic environments for the testing and training of the Waymo driver. We use machine learning to model the real world, including realistic agents (vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists etc.), roads, traffic control systems, and weather. To increase the fidelity and steerability of the simulations, we employ large foundation models, trained on our massive datasets that allow us to quickly setup and rollout multiple scenarios to subject our driver to. We are looking for research engineers to work on these exciting problems. In this hybrid role, you will report to an Engineering Manager. Role Overview 🔎 As a Senior UX Design Engineer, you'll own some of the hardest problems in our product and see them through until they're solved. You'll join our design team, three designers today and growing, and work inside our teams alongside product managers and our product, legal and AI engineers (our legal engineers are former real estate lawyers). Nobody here has the full answer yet, and that's the job: you'll get to know the people we build for, work out what they need from us, and build it. This role is not about polishing screens. Our product is live and trusted by some of the most demanding real estate lawyers and property teams in the world. The hardest design problems here are not about how it looks. Your starting point is the users, their work and the product: you notice what isn't working, decide what matters most, and see it through, from the first customer conversation to the version they use. When anyone can build, judgement matters most, and that is the heart of this role. Design how people work with our AI agents, which do real work on their behalf: what people hand over, how they check it and see where each answer came from, when they step in, what the agent asks about first and what it simply does, and how that shifts as AI improves. Solve first, then refine: get to the right answer with rough, working versions in front of real people, and add polish once the problem is solved. Build and ship interface changes yourself, using AI coding tools in our codebase. Engineering depth is welcome, not required. Keep the product coherent while everyone builds: engineers, legal engineers, product people and coding agents all build interfaces here. Explain why one option beats another so people can make the call themselves, write it down as clear, reusable rules in the codebase for agents to follow, and evolve our design system so it all still feels like one product. You bring design excellence and strong product sense: hierarchy, layout, type, copy, states, navigation and flow, and a clear view of what is worth building. You make a call and ship it without waiting for sign-off, explain it in words others can reuse, and change your mind for a good reason. You'd rather guide people than overrule them. You're genuinely excited about AI: what it can do, where it's heading and how to get the most out of it. You already design or build with AI tools, at work or in your own projects, and you want to help shape how AI changes the working day of property professionals. You want to learn how property and legal work gets done. No legal or property knowledge needed. You have owned and shipped product design work, and can walk us through the problem, not just the result. Desirable Experience designing AI products: showing the reasoning behind an answer, signalling confidence, and letting people steer an agent. Experience in legal tech, fintech, compliance or another field where precision and professional accountability shape every decision. Side projects, hackathons or things you've built outside work. Design systems and accessibility experience. Experience at an early-stage or fast-scaling startup, where there was no established process and you helped create one. Reasons we might not be for you The pace is fast and our ways of working keep evolving. If you prefer clear boundaries between design and engineering, this may not be the role for you. You'll spend most of your time on hard, unsolved problems and on building, not on perfecting polished mock-ups. Why you'll love it here You'll join a collaborative, highly ambitious team where the standard is high and the ownership is real. You'll help shape how design works in a company where AI builds alongside people. Your work is used by lawyers and property teams on real deals and real buildings. title: AI engineer (AI & GenAI) - People Domain (f/m/d)
description: Dans le cadre de l’ouverture d’un poste en CDI, nous recrutons un.e AI engineer (f/m/d) , basé-e à Paris. 🚀 CONTEXTE & ENJEUX STRATÉGIQUES Au sein de Decathlon Digital, l'équipe People Data engage une initiative majeure : transformer l'expérience de nos 100 000 collaborateurs par l'intégration de l'IA Générative et Agentique. Face à la fragmentation de l'écosystème RH dans plus de 70 pays, notre ambition est de construire une couche de simplification en s’appuyant sur les nouvelles solutions que proposent l’IA. Il s'agit d'une couche d'intelligence centralisée et agnostique des outils, capable d'interagir avec l'ensemble de notre infrastructure (Workday, Data Lake, University, ...) pour faire évoluer nos interfaces d'une logique de consultation vers une logique d'action. Dans ce cadre, nous développons DaiLY , notre agent conversationnel RH. Il aide nos collaborateurs et managers à accéder instantanément à une information fiable, sourcée à partir de notre documentation Workday et de nos politiques People. Déjà déployé avec succès en France, DaiLY entre dans une nouvelle phase de passage à l'échelle : extension internationale, industrialisation des évaluations, amélioration continue de nos modèles et de leurs qualités et déploiement et intégration d’agents autonomes RH. Pour mener ce projet, nous ne recherchons pas uniquement un.e développeur.se, nous avons besoin d'un.e " Builder " : un.e personne capable de traduire un besoin métier en solution technique, de l’implémenter, la qualifier, la déployer et la maintenir dans le temps. 🎯 VOTRE MISSION Nous recherchons un(e) AI Engineer confirmé(e) pour participer activement à l'industrialisation et au développement de DaiLY. Votre objectif est clair : transformer les besoins métiers RH en fonctionnalités IA fiables, mesurables et robustes. Pour relever ce défi, vous évoluerez au sein d'un collectif dédié , en collaboration directe avec d'autres AI Engineers, un Lead AI Engineer (qui orientera les choix d'architecture globale) et une Product Manager. Cette organisation de proximité vous permettra d'assurer une synergie parfaite entre les enjeux produits, la roadmap et l'implémentation technique. Vous aurez notamment un rôle clé dans l'évolution de DaiLY : passer d'un modèle de simple consultation (Q&A) à un véritable système agentique transactionnel capable de déclencher des actions concrètes (ex : poser des congés dans Workday, s'inscrire à des formations via Decathlon University). 🛠 VOS RESPONSABILITES Développement Agentique & Fonctionnalités Participer à l'extension des capacités de DaiLY vers des actions d'écriture (write actions) en implémentant des protocoles de tool-calling (MCP - Model Context Protocol) et des communications inter-agents (A2A). Implémenter des stratégies avancées de chunking et de re-ranking pour prioriser les règles spécifiques au domaine RH. Contribuer à l'optimisation des coûts, de la latence et de l'efficacité globale du système en lien avec les équipes Plateforme et Infrastructure. Qualité, Évaluation & Observabilité (LLMOps) Développer et maintenir la couche de qualité du pipeline RAG multi-agents (Vertex AI Search / Discovery Engine). Assurer le grounding (ancrage) des réponses et la vérification des citations pour garantir la traçabilité vers une source de vérité. Mettre en place des pipelines d'observabilité robustes pour l'évaluation online et offline (OpenTelemetry, MLflow). Coder des évaluateurs automatiques basés sur des golden datasets pour itérer sereinement et prévenir les régressions avant chaque mise en production. Intégrer des garde-fous (guardrails) pour protéger le système et les utilisateurs contre les hallucinations et les erreurs. Sécurité, Cloisonnement & Déploiement International Access Management (ACLs) : Implémenter une gestion granulaire et dynamique des droits d'accès au niveau de l'indexation et du retrieval, garantissant qu'un collaborateur n'accède strictement qu'aux documents RH de son périmètre. Isolation & Multi-tenancy : Mettre en œuvre des stratégies de filtrage par métadonnées (metadata filtering) en base vectorielle et de cloisonnement (des index et/ou des modèles) pour assurer une étanchéité parfaite des données entre les différentes sociétés fiscales, entités légales et géographies de Decathlon. Support Multilingue : Contribuer à l'architecture d'internationalisation de DaiLY en adaptant les pipelines RAG, l'embedding et l'inférence pour maintenir un haut niveau de performance et de pertinence sur une grande diversité de langues. Produit & Impact Business Aider à l'analyse des intentions des utilisateurs pour mesurer l'impact de DaiLY. Traduire, avec l'appui de la Product Manager et du Lead, les enjeux métier en comportements de modèles et en métriques de succès. 🧠 PROFIL RECHERCHE Nous recherchons un profil justifiant a minima d’une première expérience. Expérience : Profil confirmé justifiant de plusieurs années d'expérience professionnelle en entreprise (hors stages et alternances) en AI Engineering, ML Engineering ou Software Engineering orienté IA. Vous justifiez également d'au moins une expérience concrète et réussie de mise en production d'un système GenAI ou agentique. Stack Technique : Solide maîtrise de Python, de l'écosystème GCP / Vertex AI, et des frameworks d'orchestration (LangChain, LlamaIndex ou ADK). Expertise LLM & Agentique : Solide maîtrise des architectures RAG (recherche vectorielle, Vertex AI Vector Search, gestion avancée de métadonnées), mais surtout des concepts techniques agentiques : function/tool-calling, boucles de raisonnement (ReAct, etc.), orchestration de workflows multi-agents, structured output et gestion du contexte/mémoire. Qualité & Évaluation : Capacité à diagnostiquer une réponse incorrecte (problème de modèle, de retrieval ou de données) et appétence pour l'observabilité applicative (SQL / BigQuery / MLflow). Langues : Français courant obligatoire & anglais professionnel courant (environnement international). Les plus : Connaissance technique approfondie des protocoles A2A (Agent-to-Agent) et MCP. Expérience de traitement multimodal de documents ou dans des écosystèmes SIRH (ex: Workday). Compréhension technique des enjeux de sécurité (RBAC, ACLs, RGPD) appliqués aux LLMs. Connaissance des architectures microservices et conception d'APIs. 🎁 CE QUE NOUS PROPOSONS L'opportunité de développer un produit d'IA agentique de pointe avec un impact direct sur le quotidien de 100 000 collaborateurs. Un environnement technologique premium (Stack Google Cloud / Vertex AI / Databricks). Une politique de télétravail flexible (2 jours par semaine en remote, le reste dans nos bureaux à Paris - Canal de l’Ourcq). Une culture du delivery axée sur l'autonomie, l'intelligence collective et la montée en compétences (accompagnement par un Lead, certifications, formations). Des avantages attractifs (primes mensuelles/trimestrielles, actionnariat salarié). Une ambiance résolument tournée vers le sport (nombreuses corpos, tests produits, pauses déjeuner sportives ou non, …) DECATHLON DIGITAL Imaginez si la technologie nous permettait de repousser les frontières et d'offrir des expériences sportives inédites. C'est précisément notre ambition chez Decathlon Digital ! Nous sommes une équipe de plus de 5 000 experts en ingénierie logicielle, gestion de produits, données, cloud et cybersécurité, répartis à Paris, Lille et Amsterdam. Ensemble, nous créons la plus vaste plateforme sportive numérique, en exploitant les innovations technologiques pour optimiser la chaîne de valeur, concevoir des expériences connectées et donner une seconde vie à nos produits. Changeons la donne pour de bon. Notre passion du sport nous guide et nous voulons qu’elle perdure. title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Search (remote, Europe)
description: Hey, I'm Adrian . I’m hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join the Data Search team at Modash. Modash helps brands find, understand, and work with creators across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. More than 2,700 companies—including Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN—use us to manage and scale their creator partnerships. Behind that product is a fascinating search problem: helping customers find the right people across 400M+ creator profiles and billions of media files. We’re combining large-scale data processing, traditional retrieval, vector search, multimodal embeddings, and LLMs to make that possible. That’s where you come in. Why we're hiring Search at Modash isn't an internal platform or a support function. It is one of the core products customers use to discover creators. The scale is large, the data is messy, and the search intent is often complex. A customer might be looking for creators in a specific niche, people whose content conveys a certain visual style, or accounts that resemble a group they already know. Solving that well requires more than adding another filter or calling an LLM API. We need a senior engineer who can work across the full retrieval system—from data and indexing pipelines to embeddings, ranking, relevance, and low-latency serving—and take ambiguous product problems all the way to production. You’ll join the specialised Data Search team and work closely with Data Core, Data Insights, product teams, customers, and company leadership. You’ll have real autonomy, but you won’t work in isolation. If you want a feel for how we think about building software, check our Engineering Blog . What you'll actually own 1. Make creator search meaningfully better. You’ll improve how customers discover creators across 400M+ profiles and billions of media files. That includes retrieval, filtering, ranking, relevance, speed, and the product decisions that connect them. 2. Turn multimodal data into searchable intelligence. You’ll build systems that generate and use embeddings from images, video, text, and audio at massive scale—then make those signals useful in a real customer-facing search experience. 3. Ship new search capabilities into production. You’ll evaluate models and technologies pragmatically, understand tradeoffs around cost, latency, and quality, and move promising approaches from experiment to a reliable production system within weeks rather than quarters. 4. Own the system end to end. You’ll help shape the problem, gather requirements, design the architecture, write the code, release it, measure the outcome, and improve it. Senior engineers here own results, not just implementation tasks. What the day-to-day looks like Here’s what a typical week might include: Monday. A customer search is returning technically relevant but unhelpful results. You inspect the retrieval and ranking stages, identify where intent is being lost, and propose a measurable improvement. Tuesday. Deep-focus time. You build a pipeline to generate multimodal embeddings across a large batch of creator content and test how the new representation affects retrieval quality and cost. Wednesday. You work with Data Insights on a new in-house datapoint. Together, you agree on its definition, coverage, and data-quality requirements, then expose it in Search to give customers more ways to discover creators. Thursday. You test a reranking model on a fixed set of real customer queries. You measure how much it improves relevance against the latency and inference cost it adds, then decide what's ready for production. Friday. You review production metrics, investigate a relevance regression, and share what you learned with the team. The fix may be in the model, the data, the query logic, or the product itself—you follow the evidence. We keep meetings purposeful and protect time for deep work. You’ll have a short standup, close collaboration when it helps, and plenty of space to design, build, optimise, and launch. Requirements What you've done before Built large-scale data or backend products. You have solid experience working with systems where volume, latency, reliability, and cost all matter. Shipped products from concept to production. You’ve owned scoping, architecture, implementation, release, measurement, and iteration—not just one layer of the solution. Designed distributed systems. You can reason clearly about throughput, failure modes, data flow, scalability, and operational tradeoffs. Built LLM-powered or agentic features in production. You understand the practical differences between models and can balance capability against latency and cost. Worked autonomously on ambiguous problems. You know how to gather requirements, ask useful questions, and turn incomplete context into forward motion. Communicated clearly across teams. You can explain technical tradeoffs to engineers and non-engineers, give direct feedback, and collaborate without creating unnecessary process. Worked in a fast-moving product environment. You’re comfortable learning quickly, shipping incrementally, and changing direction when the evidence does. Bonus points if you’ve worked with multimodal embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, ranking algorithms, model deployment, self-hosted models, or GPU infrastructure. Curiosity about the creator economy helps too, but we’ll get you up to speed. Our stack AWS and GCP, with Pulumi for infrastructure as code Python, TypeScript, and Node.js PySpark on AWS EMR Airflow Milvus Vector DB through Zilliz Elasticsearch LLM batch APIs Apache Iceberg SageMaker, DynamoDB, S3, Glue, Kinesis, Lambda, ECS, and Aurora Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Cursor The interview process We move quickly and can complete the process in under a week: Intro chat Coding interview System design interview Team interview Culture and alignment conversation with our CEO, Avery Schrader Benefits What we offer Fully remote in Europe 🏠 Work from wherever you do your best work, with some overlap with GMT+3. Compensation. Your compensation is made up of salary and stock options. As we're growing fast, the stock option package is especially significant. Annual salary range is 100,000€ - 130,000€ for this role. We hire across Europe, so the exact number depends on your location, employment type, skills, and experience. Flexible hours ⏱ We care about outcomes, not when you log on. Unlimited paid vacation 🌴 If you’re rested and happy, you do better work. Take what you need. And we're just getting started. Over the coming decade, brand investment in creators will continue to boom, and Modash will be at the centre of it all. Modash is here to stay. We have 8-figures in ARR across two products, a $12M series A investment , and we are default alive. We are building a company that will still be here in 20 years; not rushing towards an exit. If you join Modash, you’ll be surrounded by people who truly want to be the greatest at their craft. People who make you better. title: Senior Technical Support Engineer
description: At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you. So, what’s the role all about? Any issue with our software that impairs the operation of a customer’s contact centre has significant financial ramifications for them. Our ability to restore service, improve their understanding, and resolve chronic issues will greatly increase the value they receive from our solutions and will reduce financial risk when they experience problems. How will you make an impact? Demonstrate deep subject matter expertise in our core technologies, as well as at least one other technology specialty, and develop expertise in a second area of specialty. Provide advanced technical support to customers via phone, online, chat, and email and use tools and advanced expertise to pull and effectively analyse logs, traces, packet captures, etc. to determine root cause of issues. Demonstrate professional, assertive, articulate, and friendly verbal and written communication in all aspects of your work. Take full ownership of all communication needs related to the management of troubleshooting efforts internally and externally, building confidence across all customers and stakeholders that we are progressing properly towards resolution. Effectively mentor colleagues on their communication, troubleshooting, process, product knowledge and case work. Encourage productive debate and discussion with colleagues to more thoroughly analyse and resolve problems. Be influential in improving procedures and processes that improve our efficiency and effectiveness. Ensure that each case that you own is progressing according to the response and resolution targets as specified in our Service Level Agreements (SLA). Assist colleagues in accelerating their cases toward timely resolution. Provide root cause correction, not just symptom relief. Ensure that all facets of the problem are evaluated to eliminate the recurrence of the issue. Exemplify tenacity in resolving core issues that fully resolve problems and assist peers in doing the same. Proactively manage personally assigned and cases from the queue based upon severity and priority of each issue and your skills and ability to resolve. Open and monitor incidents created with 3rd party providers. Work with other internal stakeholders to improve our interactions and success in handling these incidents. Obtain and maintain certification as a Knowledge-Cantered Service (KCS) Publisher, create useful knowledge content, and update existing knowledgebase articles using KCS methodology. Provide coaching to others on KCS best practices. Identify, document, and report issues with software, design, reliability, and maintenance issues to the proper teams, ensuring that they are aware of and are addressing customer expectations. Gather, validate, and document all pertinent details related to an issue believed to be a bug to enable the receiving R&D resource to duplicate the issue easily and rapidly. Work with R&D as needed during isolation, correction, and implementation of any delivered resolution. Develop and maintain consistent and exemplary performance on all key performance indicators, modelling a higher-level achievement for level 1 Technical Support Engineers as well as your peers at the same job level. Properly de-escalate customers through expert communication and resource engagement, ensuring that all customers that you influence are receiving excellent service. Expected to handle more complex and escalated cases. Demonstrate a deep understanding of networking technologies and how they are utilized by our products, platform, and customers. Expert at reading and analying network and other technical diagrams to aid in problem diagnosis and resolution, and often provide mentoring to colleagues to improve their technical abilities. Provide training to colleagues in real time as you perform your work and assist them in being successful in their roles. Develop training materials, best practice documentation, and other resources that will help others, including customers, to be more successful with our products. While a consistent work schedule is a norm, the ability to work a flexible schedule and provide on-call services is needed from time to time. Have you got what it takes? 5+ years’ work experience in a technical customer service role, preferably in a technical support capacity. Minimum of three years of experience working with and advanced knowledge of technologies such as SaaS, telecommunications, contact centre software, networking technologies such as TCP/IP, HTTP, SFTP, scripting, load balancers, proxies, firewalls, and Relational Databases (MSSQL, Oracle, MySQL). Excellent technical, analytical, and problem-solving skills for diverse and complex issues in high-pressure, complex, SaaS multi-platform/system/vendor environments. Excellent professional, written and verbal communications skills with the ability to capture all details in written form during conversations. Communication is assertive, articulate, and friendly while building confidence across all stakeholders you work with. Time management skills that allow you to work in a highly influential manner in an interrupt-driven environment. Ability to multi-task and maintain professional composure during stressful situations, prioritizing your activities appropriately. Superior analytical and problem-solving skills while managing diverse and complex issues in high-pressure, complex, multi-platform/system/vendor environments. Proven ability to utilize, create and update knowledgebase resources in the course of your work. Proven ability to drive escalated customer problems to resolution utilizing appropriate internal and external resources. Ability to communicate effectively across all company teams such as Product Management, Research and Development, Quality Assurance, Professional Services, and Executive/Senior Management teams to resolve technical issues. Industry experience including understanding of the contact centre business, as well as general market and business trends. Understanding of networking technologies and telecommunications architecture (PBX, Carriers, VoIP). Demonstrated ability to work independently as part of a larger team. Ability to excel in a fast-paced, agile environment with assertiveness, critical thinking, and strong problem-solving skills. Ability to adapt quickly to change, think on your feet, communicate positively and work proactively. You will have an advantage if you also have: Ability to troubleshoot VoIP, telephony/telecom technologies, DS3, Ethernet, OC-X, 1+ and toll-free services. Experience in a technical support role in a software or telecommunications environment. Workforce Management software and/or outbound dialler experience. Web Services and API knowledge and understanding of conceptual use. Competent in database and SQL concepts. Education Requirement: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Business Information Systems, Networking or a similar field, or equivalent work experience required. Requisition ID: 10964. title: Senior Software Engineer New Markets - EU
description: Who We Are: Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more. Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts. Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it. Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator. Our Team Members: We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond! We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply. Your Role: As a Senior Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining the systems and services that form Alpaca's foundation and empower millions of users who trade billions of dollars worth of assets. You will be responsible for regional recruitment initiatives, supporting cross-functional team projects, mentoring talent on our engineering principles and practices, and fostering Alpaca culture in the region. As Senior Engineer, you will also serve as the operational reliability and engineering lead and the incident commander during regional business hours, ensuring proactive 24x7 stability. For this role, we are seeking an experienced full-stack engineer dedicated to delivering high-quality, seamless software solutions. The ideal candidate has a proven track record of designing and building scalable applications and is comfortable challenging conventions and advocating for innovative solutions. In this position, you will have the autonomy to architect and implement solutions that meet our strategic objectives while also a collaborative, cross-functional team. You will also own key-management and key-hierarchy architecture across the product, ensuring interoperability with deployed HSM, TLS and IPsec ecosystems. Own the classical and hybrid cryptography architecture of the product line: symmetric, hash, RSA/ECC, entropy and key management, and classical/PQC hybrid schemes Define crypto-agility and migration mechanisms that let customers move to quantum-safe deployments without breaking existing infrastructure Requirements: We are looking for a candidate with a Master’s or PhD in Cryptography, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field and at least twelve years of experience implementing and architecting classical cryptography in real products, in hardware, software or both. You have deep command of symmetric and asymmetric primitives, modes of operation, key management and entropy generation, and you have taken cryptographic subsystems through FIPS 140-3 or Common Criteria evaluation. You also bring a solid working knowledge of the NIST post-quantum algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) and their deployment constraints: you do not need to be a lattice specialist, but you must be able to architect hybrid schemes with one. You understand the practical constraints of deployed security infrastructure (HSMs, PKI, TLS and IPsec ecosystems) and how hybrid classical/post-quantum schemes are standardised and deployed in practice. You write precise specifications, guide implementers effectively, and make sound architecture decisions under real-world interoperability constraints. Fluency in English is required; French or German is an advantage. Proven architect of classical cryptographic subsystems with certification experience (FIPS 140-3, CAVP, Common Criteria) Practical knowledge of hybrid classical/PQC schemes, crypto agility and key-management architecture, with working command of the NIST PQC standards Preferred Qualifications: You believe that quantum-safe security is only as strong as the classical foundations it stands on. title: Senior Professional Services Engineer - OX App Suite (m/f/d)
description: Our mission: Are you an engineer with real technical depth AND do you want to own the relationship with one of our major hosting customer? Working through real production problems, translating operational needs into product improvements, and filling a role that matters to both sides? This combination is rare. At Open-Xchange (OX), we develop open-source communication and collaboration software used by public sector organizations, telcos, and hosting providers to keep data secure and under their control. Our products cover email, collaboration, DNS security, and related services, and are used by millions of people worldwide. Discover what OX offers you: We work in a non-hierarchical organization that empowers everyone to take responsibility, stay focused, and contribute directly to the company’s success and customer value. We value expertise and continuous professional development. Our professionals work closely with experienced colleagues, take ownership of their work, and continuously expand their skills. Openness and diversity are core to OX. Different perspectives, backgrounds, and ways of thinking strengthen our collaboration and help us see the bigger picture. Your team: You'll work in a dedicated cell built around one of our largest hosting customers - a provider running multiple brands on OX App Suite 8. Your closest collaborators are the Account Manager and Development Engineers, with Support looped in as needed. It's a largely independent seat, but you're one of several engineers across the company running the same model for other large accounts . Your new job: Be present in the customer relationship - regular calls, occasional on-site visits, and persistent continuity that the customer's technical teams know you by name and trust your word. Build reference labs and generate reference configurations from them. Participate in OX-internal development of those frameworks. Analyze and resolve technical issues across the OX App Suite 8 stack. As L1/L2 is sitting with our customer your role is escalation-facing (L2/L3) taking ownership from escalation through to resolution and keeping the customer informed throughout. Translate customer feature requests and operational requirements into clear input for internal product and development teams, and feedback internal constraints to the customer in terms they can act on. Support the customer through upgrades, configuration changes, and new feature rollouts. Document solutions, workarounds, and deployment specifics - both for the customer and internally - and leave things better documented than you found them. Formal on-call is not part of this role. A typical day mixes customer and internal calls, hands-on lab and reference-configuration work, and technical documentation - with occasional escalation support when a customer integration needs deeper troubleshooting. Limited travel is required for customer-facing meetings (~1-2 per quarter) and company-internal meetings (~1 per quarter). This is the tech stack you'll be working with: Scale 1-5 where 5 means “hands-on depth expected on day one” and 1 means “we expect nothing and train it on the job”: OX App Suite 8 | 1 | Kubernetes (Helm-based deployments) | 5 | Mail infrastructure: Dovecot (CE / Pro), Postfix, IMAP/SMTP) | 2 | Data layer: MariaDB, Redis | 3 | Storage: Object storage (S3-compatible), Rook Ceph | 2 | Identity: Keycloak, LDAP | 2 | Observability: Prometheus, Grafana (or comparable stack) | 3 | Tooling: Linux, Bash/Python, kubectl, Helm | 5 | Networking: Istio (operational awareness, not configuration ownership) | 2 | Your background: Proven ability to hold your ground in a technical disagreement with a customer or partner, and to stay composed and credible when a large account escalates - you can point to specific situations where you did this. Solid hands-on experience with Linux-based server environments. Working knowledge of several core stack components -   mail infrastructure (IMAP/SMTP, Dovecot or equivalent). relational databases (MariaDB/MySQL). containerized deployments on Kubernetes. Familiarity with monitoring and alerting (Prometheus/Grafana or equivalent) is part of staying ahead of issues rather than just reacting to them. We don't expect OX App Suite or Dovecot experience, we train it. Practical experience troubleshooting distributed systems in production: reading logs across multiple services, correlating symptoms, and working through problems with a clear method. Comfortable writing scripts to automate operational tasks or reproduce issues. Experience in a customer-facing technical role - support engineering, professional services, or similar - where you have taken ownership of an issue or requirement from first contact through to resolution. Familiarity with Helm-based deployments and the operational patterns that come with running multi-brand or multi-tenant hosting environments. Able to work across teams and communicate technical details to people with different backgrounds: you can represent a customer's operational reality in an internal engineering discussion and translate an internal constraint back to the customer without losing either side. Clear written communication is a requirement. Documentation and knowledge transfer are part of the job. Good written and spoken English is required as is fluency in German for this particular customer relationship. This is what you get at OX: The flexibility to work 100% remotely ensures a work environment that suits you best. Flexible working hours that allow you to successfully combine your home and family responsibilities with work.  Getting together in-person for workshops and fun team events.  Time off to volunteer – and mental health support when you need it. We provide financial relief through corporate benefits and a subsidy for ergonomic chairs and desks. We can discuss further location-related benefits together in an initial talk. Join the team: Join us in our fight for an open internet and deliver added value! Click “Apply now” to submit your application. title: Propulsion Test Engineer
description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation. We are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit, and which carries cargo – and potentially humans in the long run. We are also developing different types of propulsion systems to power our future vehicles and missions. As a talented Propulsion Test Engineer , you will be responsible for the test and analysis of our future propulsion systems. Key Responsibilities: In your capacity as a Propulsion Test Engineer , your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day your duties will include: Prepare and execute tests at the engine and component level to evaluate hardware performance. Developing test plans, test objectives and schedules consistent with requirements and timelines; leading daily test operations and generating test reports. Autonomously leading risk assessment analyses and defining mitigation actions to ensure personnel and hardware safety during all test campaigns. Interpreting P&IDs and generating test sequences, balancing the risk, needs of the test and the limits of the test bench and test article. Working hand in hand with development engineers, test bench team, AIT team and external partners to support all test operations on internal and external test facilities. Supporting rapid test data processing with component development engineers to guide the remainder of the test campaign and plan future test campaigns. Defining, developing and updating test procedures and guidelines to improve test operations. Preparing technical documentation, including detailed procedures, test reports, design reviews, and performance analyses. What we would love to see from you: Bachelor's, master's or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field (master's and above preferred). 3–5 years of experience in propulsion testing or related fields. Proficiency in propulsion chemistry, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics. Proven hands-on experience with engine testing or equivalent. Background in cryogenic propulsion will be a big plus. Experience with commonly used simulation tools in propulsion testing (e.g., CEA). Proficiency in python programming language is a plus. Exposure to CAD Software (Siemens NX, CATIA, or similar) and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing. Strong problem-solving and analytical abilities. Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the ability to convey complex concepts to diverse audiences. Why you should join us! title: Propulsion Data & Modeling Engineer
description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation. The heart of a spacecraft lies in its propulsion system, and that's why we, at The Exploration Company, are dedicated to developing our own cutting-edge Propulsion Systems ensuring the highest level of efficiency and reliability in our space endeavours. We want you as a talented Propulsion Functional Systems Engineer to contribute to the development, testing, analysis, prediction and refinement of the functional architecture for Nyx Earth Propulsion System Development Models. In order to derisk and gain confidence on the flight propulsion system, different development models are being built in order to run a multitude of tests spanning from functional tests, cold flows to system level hot fires. This testing will allow for the verification and validation of all the propulsion subsystems. You will be responsible for bridging the gap between design and hardware testing for the Nyx spacecraft propulsion system. As such, you will work closely with both the design and testing teams to ensure seamless integration and validation of propulsion subsystems. You will report to the Propulsion Development Models Principal Engineer. Key responsibilities: In your capacity as a Propulsion Functional Systems Engineer, you will be responsible for the development of analysis, post processing, and prediction tools that can support testing and design activities linked to the propulsion sub-systems. Your role will be continuously evolving, but day-to-day responsibilities will include: During the Design Phase: Work closely with the pressure and feed system engineers to define the best configuration of the test setups, ensuring a high level of representativeness and testability to conduct all fluid modelling and analyses to verify repeatability of the test rigs with the flight systems and to perform test predictions. Support on the creation of test plans for propulsion subsystems (from a modeling perspective), including data acquisition, analysis, and reporting to ensure the performance of the system can be assessed. Design and develop propulsion analysis and post processing tools, to support testing activities and design maturation Work in close collaboration with the pressure and feed system engineers to ensure the anchoring of the different fluidic models and assess against test data During testing phase: Provide on-site support during propulsion test campaigns, working closely with the test operator and test conductor. Perform test campaigns, analysing in real-time, through different test parameters and ensure test results with timely resolution of any anomaly arising during testing. Conduct pre-test and post-test reviews and elaborate the test reports. Update and correlate the fluidic models based on test results. Provide actionable insights to identify key performance indicators and potential critical scenarios What we would love to see from you: A minimum of a bachelor's degree in a related Engineering discipline. +3 years of related experience in complex fluid systems, fluidic modeling, data analysis and data post processing. Strong engineering fundamentals in thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and combustion principles. Familiarity with test facilities, or storable propulsion systems is an asset Experience in propulsion systems storable or cryogenic fluidic systems is a plus. Proficiency in python for fluid analyses, data post processing and model anchoring. Experience in EcosimPro (or similar software) for the high fidelity analysis of numerical twins. Proficiency in conducting fluid analyses using classical hand calculations Excellent collaboration skills for working effectively across multidisciplinary teams. Fluency in English. Skills and Behaviours: Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong analysis and problem-solving skills. Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks. title: Staff Product Engineer
description: About Parloa Parloa’s mission is to make every customer conversation feel effortless for both customers and the companies serving them. About the role: As a Staff Product Engineer , you will work directly inside our most strategic enterprise customers. You will build the software that makes their AI agents work in production, and be measured by the difference it makes for the customer. Our agents are built by business users in Parloa’s platform, AMP. AMP already comes with a broad library of tools and integrations. Your job is the part AMP does not cover yet for a given customer: the last connection into their systems, or a capability the product does not have. Our customers are large enterprises in financial services, telecom, insurance, travel and retail. For them, a working prototype is where an engagement starts, not where it ends. The work comes in two forms. Some engagements run for years. You stay with the account, deepen its integrations and help it grow into new use cases. Others are short experiments. You test a new idea with a real customer and decide quickly whether it is worth building. At Staff level, you take on the hardest cases of both: accounts where a pilot-grade solution would fail in production, and capabilities nobody at Parloa has built before. Staff means harder problems and more ambiguity, not less hands-on work. On many accounts, you work alongside a Deployment Strategist. Think of the two of you as the account’s leadership team. The Deployment Strategist acts as its CPO and defines what success looks like. You act as its CTO and own the architecture and the build. On accounts without a Deployment Strategist, you own the engineering yourself. Areas of ownership: Lead the hardest engagements. Run complex programmes with several workstreams. Make the architecture decisions that span Parloa’s platform and several parts of the customer’s organization. Build what AMP does not cover yet. Systems of record, telephony and contact-center integrations, state management, data readiness, multi-agent orchestration and retrieval. When the answer is unclear, build a prototype quickly and decide whether it is worth pursuing before Parloa invests a full quarter in it. Own production quality and security. Evals, production readiness, observability and incident playbooks for enterprise-scale traffic. Meet the data handling standards a regulated customer expects, including PII, access control and audit trails. Debug live issues, whether they are technical or caused by model behaviour. Grow the account, and share what belongs in the product. Drive the second use case, the second business unit, the renewal. Set the delivery standard for other engineers on complex accounts. When something you build would help every customer, flag it. That is how Parloa decides what goes into the core product. Mentor other Product Engineers , and take part in interviewing and hiring. Use AI well, and set the standard for it. Decide how AI-assisted work is validated before it reaches a customer’s production traffic. Represent Parloa with senior technical stakeholders. Work directly with the customer’s principal engineers, architects and security leaders. Be the engineer commercial teams bring in when a prospect asks how the solution would work for them. What this role is not: Not running the Parloa platform itself. That is a separate engineering role. The platform is your foundation, and you build what a specific customer needs on top of it. Not agent configuration. Business users design and configure agents in AMP. You build the integrations and capabilities those agents need. Not a people-management role. You are an individual contributor and write and review code every week. OUR TECH STACK: Go, TypeScript, Node.js, Python, FastAPI, frontier LLMs, MCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka/NATS You will not use all of these, and most engagements add something new. Who you are: 8+ years of professional software development , delivering production systems end to end. Fluent in TypeScript or Python, or able to get there quickly. 5+ years leading the design and architecture of large-scale production systems in customer-facing or enterprise environments, with a focus on reliability, scale and failure modes. Experience leading agentic, spec-driven development in production. You know when a coding agent’s output is wrong and what checks it needs before it ships. A track record in long-term accounts or fast experiments. You have owned a strategic enterprise relationship over several years, through an expansion, a renewal or a leadership change. Or you have tested new ideas at the frontier and decided quickly whether they were worth building. Experience as a mentor or tech lead , helping engineers become independent. Comfortable with ambiguity and with customers. You work well in complex organizations, build trust quickly with new customer teams, spot risks early and keep your judgment when the stakes are high. Willingness to travel up to 25% to customer sites, depending on the engagement. Strong spoken and written communication skills in English. Nice to have: Experience building or deploying an LLM-powered system used by real users in production Hands-on experience with eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, prompt engineering or multi-agent orchestration (few candidates will have all of these) A founder or founding-engineer background Forward-deployed, solutions engineering, product engineering or strategic-partner experience at an enterprise software or AI company Voice or conversational AI, or contact center, telephony or CCaaS integration Experience in regulated industries such as banking, insurance or telecom Our engineering values: At Parloa, we hire, promote, and evaluate based on cultural and technical excellence. You’ll thrive here if you: Earn Trust – act with transparency and reliability. Obsess Over Customers – always start with the customer problem. Think Big – set bold goals and pursue them fearlessly. Have Integrity – do the right thing, especially when it’s hard. Disagree & Commit – debate with candor, align fast, and deliver. Own It – take full responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks. Dive Deep – master the details without losing sight of the big picture. Bias for Action – move fast, decide quickly, iterate fearlessly. Deliver Value – measure success by customer and business impact. Insist on the Highest Standards – raise the bar continuously. Go the Extra Mile – make the impossible possible. Hire & Elevate the Best – raise the bar with every hire. Our recruiting process: Recruiter Call → Technical Peer Interview → 360° Tech Interview Loop → Bar Raiser Why Parloa? We’re at the beginning of a new era in customer experience, one where AI doesn’t just respond, but understands, reasons, and takes action. We’re building agentic AI that enterprises trust with their most important customer moments: complex questions, high volumes, real stakes. When millions of people reach out to a brand, those interactions aren’t just support tickets; they’re defining experiences. We’re here to raise the standard: making every conversation seamless, intelligent, and genuinely helpful. If you care about shaping how businesses and customers connect at scale—and want your work to matter in real, everyday moments—this is where you do it. At Parloa, ownership isn’t a buzzword; it means being accountable for outcomes, not just tasks. We operate in a category that’s evolving fast, where the bar is high, and the problems are complex. We hire people who think in solutions, communicate with clarity, and follow through. People who are comfortable making decisions, taking responsibility, and raising the standard for themselves and those around them. Backed by leading global investors like General Catalyst, EQT Ventures, and Altimeter Capital, we’re scaling with a clear ambition: to become the global category leader in enterprise-grade conversational AI. We expect you to create an environment where engineers can remain highly autonomous while having clear priorities, ownership, and accountability. At the same time in this AI era we expect you to embrace new tools to shift quality and security scans left. You will: Own planning and operational execution across multiple engineering workstreams. Create visibility into priorities, dependencies, timelines, and resource allocation. Help the team turn broad technical direction into an executable roadmap. Identify and remove blockers before they significantly impact delivery. Balance new development, customer commitments, operational work, and technical debt. Define meaningful engineering metrics and use them to identify opportunities for improvement. Keep stakeholders informed about progress, risks, and trade-offs. Plan release and update cycles of the product. Maintain the product, be responsible for defects triaging and mitigation. Stay close to technology This is strictly not a purely people-management role. Technical background and experience is a must. We don't expect you to be a fluent Rust developer, we in fact are not expecting you to know Rust at all. But you should be comfortable participating in technical discussions, reviewing designs and architecture proposals, understanding engineering trade-offs, and challenging assumptions when needed. You should have a wide industry knowledge, and understand the pros and cons of different programming languages and platforms. Depending on your background and interests, you may also review code, contribute to tooling or prototypes, participate in incident investigation, or use automation and AI-assisted development to improve engineering workflows. At the same time, we do not expect the Engineering Manager to make every technical decision. Senior engineers (your team will contain a mix of engineers up to Staff and Architect levels) own significant parts of the technical direction, and a key part of the role is enabling them to do that effectively. What We’re Looking For We are looking for someone with: Significant software engineering experience before or alongside engineering management. Experience managing senior, autonomous engineers. A strong background in platform engineering, developer infrastructure, developer productivity, backend infrastructure, or distributed systems. Experience with CI/CD, release engineering, developer tooling, or internal engineering platforms. Experience owning roadmaps and delivering multi-quarter engineering initiatives. Strong understanding of software development lifecycle and engineering practices. Experience managing technical debt alongside product and business priorities. Ability to understand complex technical discussions without needing to personally own every implementation decision. Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional communication skills. Experience hiring, coaching, and developing engineers. A pragmatic approach to engineering processes: enough structure to make teams effective, without unnecessary bureaucracy. What Makes Someone Successful in This Role You are comfortable joining a team where engineers may understand individual systems more deeply than you do. Instead of trying to become the technical owner of every component, you ask the right questions, understand trade-offs, create clarity, and help engineers make good decisions together. You enjoy finding problems in the engineering system itself: unclear ownership, slow reviews, hidden dependencies, fragmented tooling, competing priorities, or processes that depend too heavily on individuals pushing things forward. You can move between a conversation about architecture or CI pipelines, a 1:1 with an engineer, roadmap prioritization with Product, and a discussion about why delivery is taking longer than expected. You are comfortable aligning your team roadmap with requirements from Product Managers, and from Engineering leadership, which may be different, and working with different stakeholders in general. Most importantly, you combine technical credibility with strong people and execution leadership. Nice to Have Experience with some of the following would be particularly relevant: Golang or Rust; understanding of WASM platform. Basic understanding of formal grammar, AST, compiler frontends. Observability and operational tooling. Open-source development. AI-assisted software development and automated code review. PostgreSQL or database infrastructure. Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, or cloud infrastructure. Multi-repository development environments. Developer-facing APIs, SDKs, libraries, or integrations. title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer - Ceph / On-Prem Cloud Storage (m/f/d)
description: Your Role You will help us build, operate and industrialize the storage foundation of our on-premise cloud platform. As part of a small, experienced team, you will own the Ceph clusters behind our block, object and file storage services – essentially the storage every customer workload eventually lands on. The platform is still actively being built, which means you will have real influence on the storage architecture, hardware lifecycle, automation strategy and technical direction. The role goes beyond Ceph itself: you will regularly work across bare metal, networking, OpenStack, Kubernetes and GitOps. As a Senior Engineer, you take ownership of your area and help make storage predictable, durable and highly automated as we scale into the petabytes Unser Tech Stack 🚀 · Ceph · OpenStack · Kubernetes · KVM · Linux · Bare Metal · Ansible · Terraform · Go · Cinder ·Neutron · Nova · RBD · Cilium · RGW/ S3 · Prometheus/ Grafana · FluxCD / ArgoCD · Git· Python · Claude Code · Cursor · Agentic Coding Tooling Your Responsibilities Design, operate and evolve our Ceph clusters for block, object / S3 and file storage - from CRUSH topology and failure domains to pool design, placement groups, erasure coding, capacity headroom and performance. Own the storage hardware lifecycle end to end – from qualification and burn-in through firmware, controller and disk health to OSD add/drain/replace, node retirement and hardware refresh. A key part of the job is automating these processes without creating tenant-visible impact. Automate the provisioning of storage nodes on OpenStack-managed bare metal , working with Ironic, RAID and disk configuration, SEDs, provider networks and VLANs. You will also own the artefact path around images, package mirrors, certificates and other dependencies needed to bring up clusters in environments with tightly controlled external connectivity. Run upgrades, rebalancing and reconfigurations as routine production operations, evolve our Infrastructure as Code and GitOps setup with Ansible, Terraform and FluxCD / ArgoCD, and make sure storage integrates cleanly with both OpenStack and Kubernetes. Own capacity planning and growth forecasting , use telemetry to understand real consumption, and build out monitoring, testing and failure-injection around performance, durability and security. AI-assisted engineering is simply part of how we work today. You use LLMs and agentic tools where they genuinely help – across development, testing, reviews, incident triage, knowledge retrieval or automation - and help us push further into self-healing and auto-remediation. Act as a technical reference and sparring partner across Ceph, storage, automation and AI tooling , document technical decisions and share your knowledge with the team. What we offer Exceptional team spirit across all departments and national borders; we live #OneTeam Exciting work in a highly innovative and international environment with cutting-edge technologies 32 vacation days, increasing with length of service Flexible working hours, home office options, and a secure permanent position with market- and performance-based compensation Employer-funded pension plan and an attractive insurance package OVHcloud covers 50% of public transportation costs Up to €400 annual financial contribution from OVHcloud towards sports activities (gym membership, sports classes, etc.) Through Corporate Benefits, you receive attractive discounts at numerous shops and companies We contribute to the leasing of your cargo bike Regular company events and free cold and hot beverages Several years of hands-on experience as an SRE, Storage Engineer or Platform Engineer running production storage infrastructure, with solid experience deploying, operating and debugging Ceph in production. You know the Ceph fundamentals from real-world operations: CRUSH, pools and placement groups, replication vs. erasure coding, BlueStore, scrubbing, recovery and backfill under load . You have managed storage infrastructure end to end , from the physical layer with drives, firmware, BIOS, controllers and hardware diagnostics through rebalancing, host drains, capacity expansion and hardware generation migrations. You are comfortable using Kubernetes as a control plane , not only as a workload runtime, and understand operators/controllers, custom resources, reconciliation and GitOps. You can also move confidently around OpenStack and debug issues involving Ironic, Neutron, Nova or Glance when needed. You have dealt with situations where durability really matters – such as degraded or near-full clusters, recovery under load or split-brain conditions – and you are used to making changes in a staged, evidence-based and reversible way. You have strong Linux and bare-metal skills , understand the block layer, filesystems and I/O behaviour, and are comfortable working with Ansible, Terraform and GitOps . AI-assisted engineering is already part of your day-to-day work. You have practical experience with LLMs and agentic tools and know where they can meaningfully support development, testing, reviews or operations. Ideally, you also bring experience with RGW / S3, RBD mirroring, CephFS or ceph-csi , deeper OpenStack storage integrations and Go and/or Python. Experience around VLAN/BGP, storage performance tuning, NVMe/BlueStore, observability, data protection, encryption, auto-remediation, security baselines or multi-site storage is also relevant for the role. You work autonomously, bring a strong sense of ownership , and are comfortable debugging problems where the actual root cause may sit somewhere between storage, networking, Kubernetes and OpenStack. You would rather verify what is happening from evidence than assume how the system should behave. We work in an international environment in English , so you should feel comfortable discussing technical topics, documenting decisions and working with the team in English. Each track operates as a mini-business, empowered with dedicated resources (e.g., product marketing, data analytics, and operational support) and direct accountability for performance.     Why this role matters at Pennylane   As Chief of Staff to the CTO, you operate as a senior leader in the Tech organisation. Your leverage does not come from managing teams but from owning the hardest problems that sit between them, and from being technical enough to earn the trust of the other engineering leaders. You are the person the CTO trusts with ambiguous, org-wide problems. You turn that ambiguity into a clear framing, a decision, an owner and a measurable outcome. This is not a coordination role. We serve 1.5m+ customers and we want to scale in Europe. At that size, the hard problems are no longer inside a squad: how the organisation plans, how it decides, how it measures itself, how it invests in foundations without stalling product delivery. That is your perimeter. You report directly to Quentin, Co-founder & CTO. Your influence comes from the scope of what you own and from credibility with senior engineering leaders, which is why we ask for a technical background. As the organisation grows, this role can evolve towards a management position. Key missions Engineering strategy and transversal initiatives Own the strategic, cross-organization initiatives that no single squad can carry: platform or architecture programmes, reliability and quality step-changes, engineering productivity, technical debt paydown Frame the problem, build the technical and business case, secure alignment across Engineering, Product and Security to drive execution Lead the Tech side of company-level programmes (e.g. European expansion, major compliance or infrastructure shifts) alongside the rest of the Tech leadership Planning & Performance tracking Own the Tech planning cycle: collect the inputs, surface the trade-offs (capacity vs. platform, run vs. new bets), and drive the arbitration with Tech leadership Drive the definition and calibration of Tech OKRs, and hold the organisation accountable Define what "good" looks like for a 70+ squad engineering organization and build the metrics that measure it (delivery cadence, reliability, quality, staffing and attrition, engineering satisfaction) Decision-making and leadership cadence Own the Tech leadership operating system: staff meetings, QBRs, roadmap and architecture reviews. You design them, set the agenda, write or commission the pre-reads, frame the decisions to be made, and make sure decisions land Maintain the CTO's decision log: what was decided, by whom, with what trade-off, and what happened next Raise the quality of decision-making across the Tech leadership team Communication Lead internal and operational communications across the engineering organization, building clear messaging systems from board decks down to team-wide updates Who you’ll work with? CTO and Tech leadership (Head of Engineering / Head of Data / Senior Engineering Managers) Rest of the leadership (CPO, VP Strategic Initiatives) Other relevant teams (e.g. Security, Finance, People) Who we’re looking for Must-have An engineering degree (engineering, computer science or equivalent scientific curriculum) Technical fluency: you can read a design doc, follow an architecture discussion, challenge an estimate or a trade-off, and be taken seriously by senior engineers 7-10 years of experience, including significant time inside a tech organisation at scale (multiple squads, platform teams), where you have lived the problems of scaling engineering A track record of owning complex, cross-organisational initiatives from framing to measurable outcome with senior stakeholders Outstanding written communication: this role produces documents that senior people act on Fluency in English Nice-to-have A hands-on engineering past: software engineer, engineering manager, Technical Program Manager, architect or equivalent Experience as a Chief of Staff, VP/Director of Engineering Operations, or in a strategy & operations function inside a product-led tech company What you can expect? Screening interview with Barbara - Senior Recruiter (30 mins) - An interview with Eric - VP Strategic Initiatives (1h) - A Business Case to prepare at home and to present (1h) - A final interview with Quentin - CTO (45 mins) What do we do to make your work life easier   🌴 Wherever you are based, you will get 25 vacations days paid by Pennylane 💵 You’ll have a competitive compensation package 📈 You'll get company shares to enjoy a piece of the success story you're building with us 🏡 You’ll have a budget to turn your home into a more comfortable workspace, as well as a monthly allowance to work from a coworking space whenever you feel like it ⛹️ Through our partner Gymlib, you’ll have access to 8000 fitness spaces in Europe and more than 300 activities related to wellness 🇬🇧 You’ll have access to Busuu to perfect your English or your French 💻 You’ll get the latest Apple equipment 🏢 Depending on the teams and the requirements of the position - title: Junior Computational Geometry Engineer
description: SAEKI - Manufacturing at software speed Europe's defense industrial base cannot respond at the speed modern conflict requires. Legacy suppliers operate on month-long timelines. Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile. SAEKI is building the operating system for autonomous factories - the infrastructure that lets Europe manufacture mission-critical components at software speed. The Role As a Junior Computational Geometry Engineer, you work on the geometry core of our Manufacturing Intelligence stack: the engine that takes an arbitrary customer CAD model, reasons about how to build it, and then proves that we built it right. You start on well-scoped parts of that engine, next to the engineers who built it, and grow into owning them. Your code runs in the factory. What We're Looking For Foundations . Degree in computer science, mathematics, mechanical engineering or a related field, with real depth in geometry, linear algebra and numerics. Internships, thesis work or serious side projects count. We do not expect years of production experience. B-rep Basics . You are comfortable with topology, NURBS, meshes and point clouds. You may never have shipped a robust boolean, and you still understand why floating-point robustness destroys naive implementations, and you want to learn how the field handles it. Kernel Exposure . You have worked with a geometry kernel and mesh libraries in at least one project: OpenCASCADE, CGAL, libigl, Open3D, PCL, Parasolid or comparable. Technical Ability . Solid modern C++ (17+) plus Python for tooling and rapid iteration. Rust is welcome. You write code others can read, test and maintain. Manufacturing Curiosity . You want to understand what happens once geometry meets a spindle, a nozzle or a fixture. CNC, additive or metrology exposure is a bonus, never a requirement. First Principles   Thinker . You reason by physics and mathematics, not analogy. When an algorithm fails on a real part, you dig until you know whether the bug sits in the code, the model or the assumption. Learning Speed . You take direct feedback, apply it immediately, and close your own knowledge gaps without waiting to be taught. Industrial Grit . You want to stand next to the machine in Germany and watch your output run. The feedback loop between your code and cutting metal is the point. On - site . Ability to work in person at our HQ in Zurich, Switzerland. What we're not looking for Researchers who want to publish and hand off. You ship. CAD users. This is a role for people who build the tools, not drive them. Engineers who need a clean spec. The problem is defined by the part, the machine, and the customer - you'll help define it. People who treat “it works on the test model” as done. Real customer CAD is broken, degenerate, and adversarial. That is the job. Engineers who are uncomfortable with ambiguity or rapidly changing priorities. What we offer Mission : Rebuild the industrial sovereignty of the West. Your work directly enables production of mission-critical hardware for defense and space. Total Ownership : High-stakes autonomy in your domain. title: Staff Windows Low Level C++ Engineer - Endpoint security
description: Our Purpose At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future.
